subject: Evaluating hosting lane for FastLane — speed vs steady-state QPS
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa@redwood.com>
To: Sam Park <sam.park@fastlane.ai>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-09-27T14:05:00-07:00
Subject: Evaluating hosting lane for FastLane — speed vs steady-state QPS

Hi Sam — thanks again for a sharp call this morning. Quick recap and proposed next steps so we stay aligned:

What we heard (product/traffic profile)
- Primary product is "Checkout+" with per-customer request latency sensitivity on the payment path. p95 goal ~120ms.
- Typical steady-state QPS: ~800 req/s across US region; predictable daily ramp with 30% peak at 11am PST.
- Short bursts up to ~2,200 req/s during flash sales (30–90s).
- Payload sizes are small (~350 tokens average) but many requests include LLM-assisted enrichment and a small synchronous rerank.

Constraints and priorities
- Latency (p95) is highest priority for front-end payment flows.
- Cost matters for batch enrichment and non-critical features.
- Security: FastLane prefers SCIM + company-managed KMS for production keys (we noted Private VPC earlier).

Initial inference hosting options we discussed
- Hosted API (Redwood Hosted): fastest path to ship; supports autoscaling and our streaming path. Good for runway and predictable cost at steady QPS, but heavy bursts could see transient throttling depending on committed tier.
- Dedicated capacity (Reserved GPUs): predictable throughput for sustained 800qps and comfortable headroom for bursts with configured burst pools and SLA-backed latency. Better fit if you require guaranteed p95 under load test.
- Private VPC / on-prem: discussed as a future step for procurement/KMS requirements; adds deployment overhead and longer lead time.

Proposed next steps
1) Technical deep-dive (90m): run by your infra and Platform SRE to validate p95 targets under a simulated 2.2k burst. Suggested attendees: Sam, FastLane SRE, Vanessa, Ben, Redwood Runtime engineer.
2) Provide a short sample QPS trace (CSV) and a small representative prompt set. We can run a 4-hour smoke test against Hosted and Dedicated pilots to show p95 delta and cost delta.
3) If results show Hosted meets p95 for 90% of windows but not burst SLOs, we propose a hybrid approach: Hosted for non-critical enrichment + Dedicated for checkout path.

I've attached a short pilot options brief and an SLO worksheet (see attachments). Please send the QPS sample when convenient.

Available times for the deep-dive next week: Tue/Wed 10–12 PT, Thu 13–16 PT. Which slot works?

Thanks,
Vanessa
VP, Strategic Accounts
Redwood Inference

Attachments:
- redwood_pilot-options.pdf (3 pages)
- SLO-matrix.xlsx (worksheet)

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-09-27T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Evaluating hosting lane for FastLane — speed vs steady-state QPS

Adding a couple of engineering notes based on the call and Vanessa's summary: 

- For steady 800 qps with p95 ~120ms we should size Dedicated at N GPUs depending on model family (we discussed gpt-like open model quantized runs). I estimate a 10–20% cost premium vs hosted at that throughput but better latency SLO guarantees.
- Bursts: if FastLane needs sub-200ms p95 during 2.2k bursts, Dedicated + burst pool is the safe choice. Hosted can absorb short bursts but under very high concurrency you'll see higher queueing and tail spikes.
- Quick experiment: we can run a 1-hour A/B against Hosted vs a small Dedicated pool using your sample trace and our continuous-batching runtime. Results should include p50/p95/p99, token cost, and a histogram of tail latencies.

I'll loop in runtime team for the deep-dive and draft the test plan. Recommended inputs from FastLane: a 1hr QPS trace (CSV), 30 representative prompts, and a target success criteria doc (what counts as pass for checkout path).

—Ben
Senior Solutions Engineer

Thanks Vanessa & Ben — this is great and aligns with what I took away. A couple of clarifying points from our SRE and procurement side:

- For the checkout path we really need p95 <= 150ms under normal traffic and ideally <220ms during short bursts. If Dedicated gives a tighter bound there that’s attractive.
- We attached a 48-hour QPS sample (fastlane_qps_sample.csv) and a brief prompt set for the enrichment path. Apologies — procurement looped me on the email; they will be on the next thread for contract questions.
- One ask from infra: can Redwood expose token-level cost estimates for the pilot run so we can compare cost-per-transaction?

Deep-dive: Tue 10:30 PT works for us. I'll invite FastLane SRE (John Li) and procurement (procurement@fastlane.ai) to the calendar invite.
